_note: DRAFT. How Kenyans hear about a policy, offline and online. A persona's channels are its media_habits plus the offline channels its rules grant. Each channel has a reach probability per event-day: the chance that an event published that day reaches a persona who uses the channel. All values are assumed until checked against audience data (e.g. Media Council of Kenya / GeoPoll audience surveys, Afrobarometer media-use items).

radio.label: radio (e.g. Radio Citizen, Ramogi, Inooro, Kameme)

tv.label: TV news (e.g. Citizen TV, NTV, KTN)

church_mosque.label: church or mosque announcements and talk

market_matatu.label: talk at the market, stage or in matatus

offline_rules.assumed: Radio is the most-used news source in rural Kenya.
Most Kenyans attend weekly religious services; refine with religion data when personas carry it.
Work happens where people talk about the news.

word_of_mouth._note: Each persona has ties drawn by code from the persona file: neighbours (same county), workmates (same livelihood profile and county), family (random, any county). Messages told to a tie arrive the next step.
